messages:
maya: Heads up — customer 'Looply' on dedicated-pool-5 is getting intermittent 429s for their production route after a quota migration at ~09:12 UTC. Spike when they hit ~50 RPS but autoscaler never scaled. Any quick ideas?

sam: @maya can you paste proxy logs + tenant config id and which route/model?

maya: route: /v1/generate model: redwood/llama-7b-prod tenant_id: looply-42 config_id: qcfg-77 plan: enterprise-dedicated

maya: ```proxy[worker-3] 2026-02-08T09:13:02Z WARN tenant=looply-42 rate_limiter=reject code=429 req_id=9f2b tokens=12 unit=RPS quota=5 allowed=5 msg=quota_exceeded```

alejandro: quota=5 RPS is definitely wrong — their SLA/plan expects 500 RPS. Did the migration change units? we had a conversion edge-case moving from per_minute -> per_second.

dina: ops-bot audit shows config change at 2026-02-08T09:11:50 by support-jen: patch qcfg-77 { quota_value: 500, quota_unit: "per_minute" } -> stored as { quota_value: 500, quota_unit: "RPS" } which yields 500 RPS vs intended 500 per minute (8.3 RPS). looks like opposite direction?

support-jen: i ran a rollback on the old plan earlier and then attempted a corrective migration script. i thought the script normalized all units but maybe i used the wrong flag. sorry — i can revert.

sam: quick check: if stored unit is RPS but downstream interprets as "tokens per 1000ms" vs our new runtime expecting "tokens per second" that could divide/multiply by 60 or 1000. can you show the tenant config from the rate-limiter service?

maya: rate-limiter config blob: ```tenant: looply-42
quota:
  value: 5
  unit: RPS
migration_meta: v2-convert-minutes-to-rps```

alejandro: ah — looks like the migration script accidentally applied a *factor* conversion in the wrong direction for tenants flagged legacy=true. 500 per minute -> (500 / 60) ~=8 RPS expected but some paths ended up converting 500 -> 500/100 -> 5 RPS. there's a /100 vs /60 bug in the conversion helper. not a noisy neighbor — the gateway is rejecting at 5 RPS so backend never sees traffic. explains no autoscale.

dina: confirmed: autoscaler metrics for dedicated-pool-5 show low CPU and queued requests at gateway level. graph: requests->gateway->rejects, backend rps flat.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily bump looply quota to expected RPS 500, 2) hotfix migration helper to correct conversion and re-run for affected tenants, 3) add regression test + feature flag for migration. who can patch rate-limiter?

sam: i'll cut a hotfix to accept legacy "per_minute" tags and treat them as per_minute until migration completes, then re-run. deploying to canary (dedicated-pool-5) first. @ops-bot please start canary deploy.

ops-bot: deploy started by sam — rate-limiter v3.4.7-hotfix -> canary group: dedicated-pool-5. CI: green. link: https://deploys.redwood/inflight/8762

sam: hotfix live in canary, monitoring logs...

alejandro: metrics: X-RateLimit-Limit header for looply now shows 500 and 429s dropped from ~120/min to ~3/min. backend rps climbed to expected levels.

maya: looply support says errors dropped and latency returned to normal. :thumbsup: Thanks team.

support-jen: i've opened ticket SUP-4923 to review the migration script, and added a post-deploy check to verify per-tenant quotas vs plan expectations. i'll own follow-up.

dina: recommend adding an alert that triggers when gateway rejects > 1% of incoming requests for a tenant AND backend utilization < 30% for 5m — would help catch gateway-level misconfigs and avoid silent autoscaler non-action.

sam: good call — i've created PR to add that alert.

maya: moving this thread to incident backlog and logging notes for postmortem. thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-128 — link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-128
